samples.summary: Undo floor now retains a live reference to the initial-load history entry (full-document reverse ops), keeping document content resident for the store's lifetime
samples.evidence: `undoFloorMark: UndoStackEntry | null` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:588, set in `markUndoFloor()`) replaces a plain integer with a strong reference to the `HistoryOperation[]` produced by the initial `writeFullDocument` update. That entry contains the reverse operations of the whole loaded document, i.e. document text. Because the field is held on the store, the entry cannot be garbage-collected even after Yorkie's 50-entry cap `shift()`s it off the undo stack, and it survives for the whole session/store lifetime (there is no clearing on teardown or on `replaceDocument`). Impact is limited — the same content is already in the CRDT in the same process — so this is memory/sensitive-data retention hardening rather than an exploitable exposure. Attack chain not completed: I found no path where another origin or user can read that heap state.

samples.summary: Batching every selection-replacing edit into a single doc.update() makes one client action produce one unbounded Yorkie change, which can exceed the SDK/server change-size limit and fail the whole edit (availability)
samples.evidence: `withUndoUnit()` (text-editor.ts:~3796) wraps `deleteSelection()` and the composite edit paths (typing, paste `applyPastePlan`, Enter, page break, `pastePlainTextFromClipboard`) in `Doc.batch()` → `YorkieDocStore.batch()` → a single `this.doc.update(...)` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:2929). Previously a select-all delete over an N-block document was N separate changes; it is now one change whose size grows with N. The repo already records this failure mode for a different feature: docs/tasks/archive/2026/08/20260801-board-miro-import-lessons.md:227 — "5000 elements in one Yorkie change can hit the SDK's document-size limit; consider chunking above a threshold." A user (or an attacker who can get a large document/paste in front of a victim editor) can therefore make a routine Cmd+A + type reject the whole change; `Doc.batch()` re-reads the store on throw so no data is lost, but the edit is silently dropped and the session can become unable to apply that operation. I did not confirm an actual size threshold in the pinned SDK version, hence low confidence; no per-change size guard or chunking exists on this path.
